questions.question: The process of covering bare ground with a layer of organic matter in order to retain soil moisture is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mulching**__.

__
 
• **Mulching** is the process of covering the bare ground with a layer of organic matter in order to retain soil moisture.

 Mulching is a protective layer of a material that is spread on top of the surface of the soil.

 Mulching helps in the conservation of soil moisture, improving the fertility of the soil, and reducing weed growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Contour ploughing **is the farming practice of plowing or planting across a slope following the contours of hills and slopes.
 
• These contour lines create a water break which reduces the formation of rills and gullies during times of heavy water run-off; which is a major cause of soil erosion.
 
• The water break also allows more time for the water to settle into the soil. 
 
• In contour ploughing, the ruts made by the plough run perpendicular rather than parallel to slopes, generally resulting in furrows that curve around the land and are level.​
 
• **Terrace farming** is a farming technique whereby “steps” known as terraces are built onto the slopes of hills and mountains.
 
• 
 
 
• This practice is mainly used on sloping lands to prevent rainfall-runoff and to reduce serious erosion.
 
 
 
• **Intercropping** is the practice of cultivation of two or more crops simultaneously on the same field. 
 
 
• Inter-cropping helps in increasing soil fertility and also helps in the prevention of pests and diseases to spread throughout the field.

questions.question: Where in India is the ‘slash and burn’ agriculture known as ‘Kuruwa’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State of Jharkhand.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **In the state of Jharkhand, the ‘slash and burn’ agriculture is known as ‘Kuruwa’.**
 
• It is prevalent in the tropical region in different names:
 
 
• Jhuming in Northeastern states of India,
 
• Milpa in Central America and Mexico,
 
• Roca in Brazil,
 
• Ladang in Indonesia and Malaysia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In primitive subsistence agriculture or shifting, cultivation vegetation is usually cleared by fire, and the ashes add to the fertility of the soil.

 
 
• This is also called slash and burn agriculture.
 
 
 
• The cultivated patches are very small and cultivation is done with very primitive tools such as sticks and hoes.
 
• After some time (3 to 5 years) the soil loses its fertility and the farmer shifts to other parts and clears another patch of the forest for cultivation.
 
• The farmer may return to the earlier patch after some time.

questions.question:
Given below are the names of three states:

(a) Punjab,

(b) Haryana,

(c) Odisha.

In which of the given states is rice a subsistence crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Only (c).__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Odisha, **rice** is a **subsistence crop.** 
 
• The crops which are grown to meet the needs of themselves (farmers) and their families are **called subsistence crops.**
 
• In Odisha, the soil is mostly loamy or sandy and rice cannot be grown to a large extent and is only a subsistence crop.
 
• A simple **example** of subsistence farming is a family growing grain and using that grain to make enough bread for themselves, but not to sell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The crops which give better refunds to the farmers are called **commercial crops.** 
 
• **Commercial farming** is a method where the crops and livestock are raised to sell products in order to make money.
 
• Rice is a commercial crop in the states like Punjab, Haryana, etc.
 
• A commercial crop is typically purchased by parties separate from a farm.
 
• **Tobacco** is an example of commercial farming.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about forests in INCORRECT?

options.text: In a forest, trees form the uppermost layer of vegetation.
Forests protect the soil from erosion.
In a forest, shrubs form the lowest layer of vegetation.
Forests influence climate, water cycle and air quality.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'In a forest, shrubs form the lowest layer of vegetation.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Forest Vegetation Layers:**

 
 
• Forests have a structured layering of vegetation. The layers, from top to bottom, include the canopy, understory, herb layer, and the forest floor.
 
• The uppermost layer is the **canopy**, formed by the crowns of tall trees.
 
• The **understory** is beneath the canopy and consists of smaller trees and shrubs.
 
• The **herb layer** is closer to the ground and includes grasses, ferns, wildflowers, and other herbaceous plants.
 
• The **forest floor** is the bottom layer, consisting of decomposing leaves, twigs, and organic matter.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Trees Form the Uppermost Layer:**

 
 
• Trees forming the uppermost layer of vegetation create the forest canopy, which is crucial for various ecological functions including providing habitat and influencing microclimate.
 
 
 
• **Forests and Soil Erosion:**
 
 
• Forests play a significant role in protecting soil from erosion through their root systems and ground cover, which stabilize the soil and prevent runoff.
 
 
 
• **Forests Influence Climate, Water Cycle, and Air Quality:**
 
 
• Forests have a major impact on the climate by absorbing carbon dioxide, influencing precipitation patterns, and through evapotranspiration processes.
 
• They also play a crucial role in the water cycle by facilitating the infiltration of water into the soil and maintaining watershed health.
 
• Forests contribute significantly to air quality by acting as carbon sinks, producing oxygen, and filtering pollutants from the air.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The lowest layer of vegetation in a forest is typically called the herb or ground layer, composed of low-growing non-woody plants like grasses, ferns, and mosses.
 
• Shrubs are usually found in the understory layer, which is above the ground layer but below the canopy.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions could harm tea plantations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Temperature above 35°C. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Conditions required for tea plantations:**
 
• Well-distributed rainfall of around **150-300 cm** is considered suitable for successful tea production.
 
• The monthly average maximum temperature range between 28°C and 32°C during April to September.
 
 
• **Hence ****Temperature above 35°C is harmful.**
 
 
 
• As far as soil conditions are concerned, generally, sandy loam to silty loam type of soil with a pH range of 4.5-5.5 is ideal for growing tea.
 
• Tea is a **shade-loving plant** and develops more vigorously when planted along with shady trees.
 
• Soil should possess a minimum of 1% of organic carbon, 1-2% of organic matter, 35ppm of P2O5 and K2O for the successful establishment of tea.
 
• Planting of tea is done either in spring (June-July) after the first few showers of rain or in autumn (October-November) while the soil is still moist and the area has irrigation facilities.

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes “endemic species”?

options.text: Species with less population may move to the category of endangered species.
Species that are not found existing after intense searches.
Species that are found only in some particular areas.
Species that have come from abroad.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **3 **i.e __**Species that are found only in some particular areas.**__

 
• Species that are found only in some particular areas are called endemic species.
 
• Endemic species can easily become extinct or endangered from the earth.
 
• **The dodo** is an extinct flightless bird that was endemic to the island of Mauritius, in the Indian ocean.
 
• Dodo is an example of the vulnerability of endemic species to habitat alteration.
 
• Important Endemic specie in India are:
 
 
• Asiatic Lion in Gir Forest.
 
• Nilgiri Tahr in Nilgiri Hills.
 
• Sangai Deer in Loktak Lake.
 
• Purple Frog in the Western Ghats.
 
• Kashmir Stag in Kashmir Valley.
 
• Lion Tailed Macaque in the Western Ghats.
 
• Pygmy Hog in Assam.
 
• Malabar Civet in the Western Ghats.

questions.question: A system in which local farmers were allowed to cultivate temporarily within a plantation is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__taungya cultivation__**.

 
• Taungya is a system originating in **Burma**. In the initial stages of an orchard or tree plantation, trees are small and widely spaced. The free space between the newly planted trees accommodates a seasonal crop.
 
• **Shifting cultivatio**n is an agricultural system in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned while post-disturbance fallow vegetation is allowed to freely grow while the cultivator moves on to another plot.
 
• **Intensive agriculture, also known as intensive farming **and industrial agriculture, is a type of agriculture, both of crop plants and of animals, with higher levels of input and output per cubic unit of agricultural land area.
 
• **Extensive farming or extensive agriculture** is an agricultural production system that uses small inputs of labor, fertilizers, and capital, relative to the land area being farmed.

questions.question: Amul is a success story of cooperatives in milk and milk products from _______, which brought in the White Revolution in the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat.**__

__
 
• **Amul was founded in 1946 in Anand, Gujarat with a mission to prevent the exploitation of the farmers by middlemen.**
 
• The Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation Ltd manages Amul.
 
• Amul spurred the **White Revolution in India, which placed India at the highest of milk-producing nations.**
 
• Amul is present in over 50 countries, and India alone has quite 7200 exclusive parlors.
 
• **In 1999, Amul was awarded the “Best of All” Rajiv Gandhi National Quality Award“ for maintaining the utmost quality in its plants.**
 
• **Amul has been awarded the Guinness record for the longest-running advertising campaign.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **White Revolution in India:**

 
 
• The Government of India initiated **Operation Flood known as the White Revolution after witnessing the huge success of the Green Revolution, which resulted in an immense increase in wheat and rice production.**
 
• The white revolution in India started with the motive of accelerating milk production to make the country one of the largest producers of milk in the world.
 
• It created a national milk grid linking producers throughout India to consumers in over 700 towns and cities and reducing seasonal and regional price variations while ensuring that producers get a serious share of the profit by eliminating the middlemen.
 
• Today, India is the world’s largest producer of milk, and** Dr. Verghese Kurien is known as the father of the White Revolution in India.**

questions.question: Who among the following has developed Madhuban Gajar, a biofortified carrot variety with high β-carotene and iron content?

The production and marketing of seeds of the variety are taken care of by his **son Shri Arvindbhai**.
